questions.knowledge_point: Computing One Step Using the Trapezoidal Method
questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=-2x+y,\,y(1)=0
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step to approximate $y\,(\frac{3}{2}),$ rounded to two decimal places

$$
y\,(\frac{3}{2})≈{{field-1}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=\frac{3}{2},$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=\frac{3}{2}-1=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-2x+y+(-2{x}_{\text{new}}+{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(-2x-2{x}_{\text{new}}+y+{y}_{\text{new}}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(-2x-2{x}_{\text{new}}+y)+\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{4}(-2x-2{x}_{\text{new}}+y)+\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{4}(-2x-2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y)+\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{4}(-2x-2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{3}(-2x-2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=1+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{3}{2}.$ Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{3}(-2x-2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(-2\cdot 1-2\cdot \frac{3}{2}+5\cdot 0) \\  & =-\frac{5}{3} \\  & ≈-1.67.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y\,(\frac{3}{2})≈-1.67.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=y(3{e}^{x}-2),\,y(0)=-1
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step to approximate $y(1),$ rounded to two decimal places.

$$
y(1)≈{{field-1}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=1,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=1-0=1.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(y(3{e}^{x}-2)+{y}_{\text{new}}(3{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}-2))\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,y(3{e}^{x}-2)+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(3{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}-2).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{2}\,y(3{e}^{x}-2)+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(3{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}-2) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{3}{2}\,y{e}^{x}+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(3{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}}-\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(3{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}-2) & =\frac{3}{2}\,y{e}^{x} \\ \frac{1}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}(4-3{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}) & =\frac{3}{2}\,y{e}^{x} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{3y{e}^{x}}{4-3{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=0+1=1.$ Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{3y{e}^{x}}{4-3{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}} \\  & =\frac{3\cdot (-1)\cdot {e}^{0}}{4-3{e}^{1}} \\  & =\frac{-3}{4-3e} \\  & ≈0.72.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y(1)≈0.72.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=y({e}^{x}+1),\,y(0)=1
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step to approximate $y\,(\frac{1}{2}),$ rounded to two decimal places.

$$
y\,(\frac{1}{2})≈{{field-1}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=\frac{1}{2},$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=\frac{1}{2}-0=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(y({e}^{x}+1)+{y}_{\text{new}}({e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}+1))\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\,y({e}^{x}+1)+\frac{1}{4}\,{y}_{\text{new}}({e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{4}\,y({e}^{x}+1)+\frac{1}{4}\,{y}_{\text{new}}({e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}+1) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{4}\,y({e}^{x}+5)+\frac{1}{4}\,{y}_{\text{new}}{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}+\frac{1}{4}\,{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}}-\frac{1}{4}\,{y}_{\text{new}}{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}-\frac{1}{4}\,{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{4}\,y({e}^{x}+5) \\ \frac{1}{4}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(3-{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}) & =\frac{1}{4}\,y({e}^{x}+5) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{y({e}^{x}+5)}{3-{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=0+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}.$ Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{y({e}^{x}+5)}{3-{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot ({e}^{0}+5)}{3-{e}^{1/2}} \\  & =\frac{6}{3-{e}^{1/2}} \\  & ≈4.44.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y\,(\frac{1}{2})≈4.44.$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing Two Steps Using the Trapezoidal Method
questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=2x+3y,\,y(-1)=0
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with two steps to approximate $y(0)$ and $y(1),$ rounded to two decimal places.

$$
y(0)≈{{field-1}},\,y(1)≈{{field-2}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, note that we are given $y(-1)$ and asked to find $y(1).$ The distance from $x=-1$ to $x=1$ is $2,$ and since we are asked to use two steps of equal size, our step size must be

$$
Δx=\frac{1-(-1)}{2}=1.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((2x+3y)+(2{x}_{\text{new}}+3{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2x+2{x}_{\text{new}}+3y)+\frac{3}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{2}(2x+2{x}_{\text{new}}+3y)+\frac{3}{2}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{2}(2x+2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y)+\frac{3}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{2}(2x+2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =-(2x+2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y)\end{aligned}
$$

We now proceed to calculate our approximations of $y(0)$ and $y(1).$

**Step 1**.

From the initial conditions, we have

$$
x=-1,\,y=0.
$$

Therefore, the new $x$ value is 

$$
{x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=-1+1=0.
$$

Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =-(2x+2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y) \\  & =-(2\cdot (-1)+2\cdot 0+5\cdot 0) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**.

From the previous step, we have

$$
x=0,\,y=2.
$$

Therefore, the new $x$ value is 

$$
{x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=0+1=1.
$$

Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =-(2x+2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y) \\  & =-(2\cdot 0+2\cdot 1+5\cdot 2) \\  & =-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
y(0)≈2.00,\,y(1)≈-12.00.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=-3x-y,\,y(0)=3
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with two steps to approximate $y\,(\frac{1}{3})$ and $y\,(\frac{2}{3}),$ rounded to two decimal places.

$$
y\,(\frac{1}{3})≈{{field-1}},\,y\,(\frac{2}{3})≈{{field-2}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, note that we are given $y(0)$ and asked to find $y\,(\frac{2}{3}).$ The distance from $x=0$ to $x=\frac{2}{3}$ is $\frac{2}{3},$ and since we are asked to use two steps of equal size, our step size must be

$$
Δx=\frac{\frac{2}{3}-0}{2}=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((-3x-y)+(-3{x}_{\text{new}}-{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(-3x-3{x}_{\text{new}}-y)-\frac{1}{6}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{6}(-3x-3{x}_{\text{new}}-y)-\frac{1}{6}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{6}(-3x-3{x}_{\text{new}}+5y)-\frac{1}{6}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{6}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{6}(-3x-3{x}_{\text{new}}+5y) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{7}(-3x-3{x}_{\text{new}}+5y)\end{aligned}
$$

We now proceed to calculate our approximations of $y(\frac{1}{3})$ and $y(\frac{2}{3}).$

**Step 1**.

From the initial conditions, we have

$$
x=0,\,y=3.
$$

Therefore, the new $x$ value is 

$$
{x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=0+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{7}(-3x-3{x}_{\text{new}}+5y) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}(-3\cdot 0-3\cdot \frac{1}{3}+5\cdot 3) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**.

From the previous step, we have

$$
x=\frac{1}{3},\,y=2.
$$

Therefore, the new $x$ value is 

$$
{x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{2}{3}.
$$

Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{7}(-3x-3{x}_{\text{new}}+5y) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}(-3\cdot \frac{1}{3}-3\cdot \frac{2}{3}+5\cdot 2) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
y(\frac{1}{3})≈2.00,\,y(\frac{2}{3})≈1.00.
$$
